$comment: template: translate-progress; purpose: Track per-chapter translation progress for resume across failed/incomplete sessions; phase: writing; consumers: [book-writer, master]
title: Translation Progress Ledger
description: Schema for books/<slug>/.translate-progress.json — append-only resume file.

chapters.description: Chapter filename (with extension) to progress record.

parts_written.description: Number of chunked-write parts successfully written so far.

expected_parts.description: Total parts planned per the chunked-write protocol (1 for files ≤20KB).

last_byte_offset.description: Byte offset in the target file at which the next resume should continue.

last_line_number.description: Line number at which the next resume should continue (1-indexed).

session_id.description: The session that wrote the last successful part. Used to detect session-stuck states.

started_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when this chapter's first part was written.

last_updated.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the most recent part.

checksum.description: SHA-256 of the partial chapter file at last_updated time.

glossary_gaps.description: Terms reported as missing from the source by this chapter's session.

notes.description: Free-text notes from the writer for the next session.

ch-04-reflection.md.notes: Stopped mid-H2 'Implementation examples'. Next part starts at line 199.

x-open-questions: Should expected_parts be derived from source size at dispatch time, or set by the writer on first write?
Should `glossary_gaps` be auto-merged into glossary.md, or kept as a writer-side todo?
How long after last_updated should a session be considered 'stuck' (for the monitoring slice)?
